login.title: Sign in to DSMS
login.failed: Wrong username or password. Check the keyboard layout, Caps Lock, and that the browser did not fill in an old saved password — type it by hand.
login.locked: Too many failed attempts: sign-in from your address is blocked. Wait {minutes} min and try again — more attempts will not help now.
login.serverError: The panel answered with error {status}. It is not the password: check that the panel service is running and the reverse proxy can reach it.
login.unreachable: The panel does not respond. It is not the password: check the network and that the panel service is running.
login.cookieLost: The password is correct, but the browser did not keep the session. This happens when the panel is opened over http:// — open it over https://.

resources.secretHint: The value is sent to Docker once and can never be read back.
resources.secretsNote: Docker secrets are write-only: their values cannot be shown or edited by design. To change a secret, remove it and create a new one, then update the services that use it.

disk.allImages: also remove tagged images (all images without containers)
disk.pruneHint: Will be removed: {what}. This frees {size}. Running services are not affected.
disk.noAgents: No agents have reported yet — disk usage is unavailable.
disk.explain: “Will free” is calculated per image layer: a shared layer is counted once, and a layer needed by a running image is not counted at all. So the number is smaller than the sum of image sizes, but it matches what the cleanup really frees. “Clean up everything” removes containers, images, build cache and anonymous volumes in that order — this frees more than the buttons one by one.
disk.keptHint: Unused named volumes: {size}. Cleanup does not remove them — they hold service data. A volume can be removed in “Resources → Volumes”.
disk.pruneHintApprox: Will be removed: {what}. This frees at least {size}. Running services are not affected.
disk.totalAtLeast: will free in total at least
disk.laterHint: {size} more is freed only by “Clean up everything”: these image layers are held by stopped containers and the build cache.
disk.pruneAllConfirm: Clean up everything unused on node {node}?
disk.pruneAllHint: Will be removed in order: stopped containers, {images}, unused build cache, unused anonymous volumes. This frees {size}. Running services and named volumes are not affected.
disk.pruneAllHintApprox: Will be removed in order: stopped containers, {images}, unused build cache, unused anonymous volumes. This frees at least {size}. Running services and named volumes are not affected.

logs.emptyResult: No lines returned for tail={tail}. Try a smaller value; the panel's own logs will show the reason.

services.name: Name
services.stopConfirm: Stop service {name}? (scale to 0, replicas will be remembered)
services.deployHint: The panel will re-pull the latest image for the current tag and roll the service using its stack's update policy (order/parallelism).
services.deployStarted: Deploy started — updating in the background
services.removeHint: Type the service name «{name}» to confirm removal.
services.noTasksStopped: The service is stopped — no tasks. Start it from the services list.
services.notFoundHint: It may have been removed, or the link is outdated.

replicasHint.over: That is more than needed: the service update has not finished and old tasks were not removed. Check the service tasks; “Redeploy” usually helps.
replicasHint.under: That is fewer than needed: some tasks did not start. See the service tasks and logs for the reason.
replicasHint.stopped: The service was stopped from the panel. “Start” restores the previous replica count.

stacks.name: Stack
stacks.redeployConfirm: Force redeploy all services of stack {name}?
stacks.deployHint: For each service in the stack the panel will re-pull the latest image for the current tag. The rollout follows the stack's compose update policy and may take a while.
stacks.deployStarted: Stack deploy started — updating in the background
stacks.removeHint: This removes all {count} services of the stack along with its networks, secrets and configs. Data volumes are kept. This cannot be undone.
stacks.stopHint: All services of the stack will be stopped (scale 0). Replica counts are remembered — “Start” brings them back. Global services cannot be stopped this way: they keep running.
stacks.removeLabel: Type the stack name to confirm
stacks.notFoundHint: It may have been removed, or the link is outdated.
stacks.resourcesHint: “External” means the object was not created by this stack and stays when the stack is removed. Volumes are never removed with a stack.
stacks.noServicesManaged: The stack has no services: the deploy failed or the services were removed. Open “File” and deploy it again — or remove the stack.

op.startNothing: Stack {name} has no services stopped by the panel
op.globalSkipped: Global services were not stopped (they have no replicas): {names}

stackDeploy.dotenvHint: Contents of the .env file (one KEY=value per line) — substituted into ${'{'}VAR{'}'} in the YAML:
stackDeploy.prune: Remove services no longer in the file (careful!)
stackDeploy.registryHint: Credentials from Settings → Registries: the panel passes them to Docker when pulling this stack's images and remembers them for “Deploy stack”.
stackDeploy.changeRemoveHint: will be kept — enable prune to remove
stackDeploy.missingTitle: Missing external resources — create them first
stackDeploy.warningsTitle: Not transferred to Swarm — check before deploying
stackDeploy.doneWithWarnings: Deployed, but {count} setting(s) were not transferred

help.intro: Variables in the YAML are substituted at deploy time. How it works:
help.step2: 2. Set their values on the «Variables» tab (.env field or manual pairs):
help.step3: 3. On deploy the placeholders are replaced:
help.tipDefault: The :- form sets a default value when the variable is not set.
help.tipOverride: Manual pairs override whatever is set in the .env field.
help.tipMissing: If a variable is missing and has no default — it becomes empty.

settings.refreshHint: How often agents collect and send metrics (1–30 s). This is a server setting — each agent picks it up within ~10 s. Controls the update rate of all live charts.
settings.tokenRotation: Agent token rotation (Docker CLI on a manager node)
settings.regWhat: Credentials for private Docker registries (Docker Hub private, ghcr.io, GitLab, your own). Needed only if your services pull images from a private registry — then pick the registry when updating a service image. For public images you don't need this.
settings.backupHint: The panel database holds stack sources, encrypted env values, users and audit — none of this exists anywhere in the cluster. Keep the DSMS_ENCRYPTION_KEY secret separately: without it the encrypted values in a backup cannot be read.

nodes.rotateConfirm: Old tokens will stop working immediately.
nodes.drainConfirm: Drain the node? All tasks will be moved to other nodes.
nodes.removeConfirm: Remove this node from the cluster?
nodes.forceRemoveConfirm: Node is not down! Force-remove it from the cluster?

usage.cpuHint: CPU: 100% = one fully busy core (same as docker stats).
usage.netHint: Receive (↓) and transmit (↑) rate: sum over all tasks, loopback excluded
usage.partial: Incomplete data: metrics came from {got} of {total} tasks.
usage.memHint: RAM: memory in use right now (without file cache, like docker stats). The second line is the limit, if set.

noData.title: No usage data: tasks are running, but no metrics arrived.
noData.silent: the node agent sends no metrics (not running or cannot reach the panel)
noData.outdated: the node agent is outdated — update the agent service to the panel version
noData.failed: the node agent could not query Docker — see the agent logs
noData.unseen: the agent has not reported this task yet (it has just started)
